Subject: Re: Rapid p95 jump across hosted-api since 07:55 — seeing request queueing

Triage notes (runtime on-call):

Observations:
- Around 07:50 we see a change in batching behavior on a subset of hosted-api nodes: average batch size increased by ~3x for the model family serving FinApps (same model, different batch hint).
- KV cache hit rates unchanged; CPU/GPU utilization is moderately higher but not saturated.
- Queue depth rose sharply leading to prioritized long-tail requests being pushed to p95/p99.

Preliminary root cause hypothesis: a client-side burst combined with an aggressive batching policy (continuous batching thresholds) caused larger batches and longer wait times for queued requests — increasing tail latency.

Actions taken:
- Temporarily lowered batch window for the affected shard to reduce batching delay.
- Pulled the request sample (attached) for replay analysis.
- Opened INF-4321 for follow-up on batching threshold defaults and per-tenant throttles.

Attachments: request-log-sample.gz

Markus Klein
Runtime & Inference Engineering
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: FinApps Ops <ops@finapps.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-07T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Rapid p95 jump across hosted-api since 07:55 — seeing request queueing

Hi Jane / team —

Short interim mitigation we applied:
- Reduced batch window (runtime) on the FinApps-serving pool — immediate p95 improvement from ~1.8s to ~480ms on the next 10 minutes of traffic.
- Enabled per-tenant soft limit to shed low-priority background traffic.

Recommended next steps for FinApps (action items):
1) If possible, add a small jitter to client request timings to avoid synchronized bursts.
2) Consider adding a lightweight client-side rate-limit/backoff when 5xxs are observed.
3) Share any recent deployment or traffic pattern changes that could explain a sudden burst.

We’ll continue monitoring and Markus’ team will run a replay against our staging runtime to confirm the batching threshold fix.

Monica Patel

Folks — closing the loop for the day with an executive summary and next steps. Copying Sean and Hannah for visibility and any guidance on commercial remediation.

Summary (what happened):
- At ~07:45 FinApps rolled a change that increased request burstiness. Combined with an aggressive continuous-batching configuration on the served shard, this produced larger-than-expected batches and increased queue waiting time — driving p95/p99 regressions and some 503s.

What we did (short-term):
- Reduced batch window on affected pool (immediate p95 improvement).
- Temporarily enabled per-tenant soft-shed to protect latency-sensitive traffic.
- Opened INF-4321 to track durable fixes (batching thresholds, per-tenant configuration safeguards).

Follow-up (next 48 hours):
- Markus to replay the request sample and validate that the batching change is the cause and that default thresholds are safe across typical traffic shapes (INF-4321).
- Runtime team to add a per-tenant watchdog that automatically relaxes batching when queue depth crosses SLO thresholds.
- CS/Account to propose a customer remediation (temporary credits / service adjustment) and coordinate comms.

Financial / commercial ask: Monica / Sean — advise on typical credit ranges for a partial-day outage impacting tail latency. FinApps has a committed usage profile under deal D-2029-FA-78.
